segments.caption: Flooline: a flood-mapping copilot. Saved real satellite inputs and pre-event OpenStreetMap; this walkthrough does not acquire new imagery.
Before and after Sentinel-1 observations use compatible radar geometry. Historical OSM and source dates stay attached to this analysis.
Water assessment covers 13.6% of this area. Debris needs usable paired optical observations. Results describe assessed areas; other areas remain unknown.
Ask a compound English question. The copilot retrieves mapped water and observation coverage. The displayed engine identifies Groq or the deterministic fallback actually used.
Clicking a citation opens the exact fact, source path and method. Area-wide measurements refer to the selected analysis, rather than an invented map location.
Access results distinguish uncertain, unassessed and baseline-disconnected settlements. A missing observed route does not automatically mean a village was cut off by flooding.
Settlement details link modeled routes, destination-specific hospital evidence and unverified connectors. Water below a bridge does not establish bridge failure or a confirmed road closure.
Switch to Nepali and ask about observation coverage. Saved values and uncertainty remain unchanged; native-speaker terminology review is pending.
The evidence panel exposes fact IDs and canonical values. Matching saved facts verifies numerical consistency; it does not verify physical mapping accuracy.
Inspect Data & method: recorded satellite inputs, elevation and historical OpenStreetMap stay attached to the selected analysis.
Generate a Nepali situation report using validated narrative and selected map facts. HTML, PDF and JSON preserve the snapshot, source dates, partial coverage and attribution.

The one-page report explicitly marks cached real inputs, incomplete observations and unavailable debris. Nepali text uses bundled Devanagari fonts; the report needs independent field and language review.
EMSR927 is evaluation-only. Its landslide references have no eligible debris observations here, so accuracy is N/A. A class mismatch or empty comparison is never presented as a perfect score.
Educational prototype, not operational. Field verification and native Nepali review remain necessary. The copilot uses a hosted model; this application trains no model.

replies.question: How much new water was detected, and how much of the area was eligible?
replies.answer:

Unobserved areas remain unknown. No mapped change does not prove absence of damage.
Surface-change/debris candidates can include other land-cover changes; they are not confirmed debris flows.
